macros.name: abovebaseline
macros.doc: The macros \abovebaseline and \belowbaseline also creates the means to shift an item’s baseline.

macros.name: addstackgap
macros.doc: The \addstackgap macro provides a user-requested feature to add a specified gap above and below an object.

macros.name: Centerstack
macros.doc: The macro \Centerstack produces a type of \Longstack that is vertically centered about the mid-strut above the baseline.

macros.name: ensurestackMath
macros.doc: The macro \ensurestackMath{} macro is used to force its argument (a stacking command) to be processed in math mode, without setting the global default stacking mode to math mode (accomplished via \stackMath).

macros.name: Longstack
macros.doc: The \Shortstack and \Longstack commands are stacking commands that allow more than two stacking rows to be specified at once.

macros.name: quietstack
macros.doc: The parameter \quietstack defaults to “F” (false) and determines whether the result of a stacking operation is suppressed from the output.

macros.name: savestack
macros.doc: The macro \savestack provides a means to save an intermediate result (in a box that can be recalled with the specified macro) without printing it.

macros.name: setstackEOL
macros.doc: The \setstackEOL macro allows the end-of-line (EOL) character to be defined to a more convenient setting, such as \\, though any character will work.

macros.name: Shortstack
macros.doc: The \Shortstack and \Longstack commands are stacking commands that allow more than two stacking rows to be specified at once.

macros.name: Sstackgap
macros.doc: For short stacks, the default stacklength, stored in \Sstackgap, is 3pt, which corresponds to the same spacing found in TeX’s \shortstack command.

macros.name: stackalignment
macros.doc: The parameter \stackalignment defaults to “c” (center) and defines the default stacking alignment.

macros.name: stackanchor
macros.doc: The \stackanchor macro is one way to create a stack where the baseline is split between two items in the stack.

macros.name: stackengine
macros.doc: The basic (and most general) stacking macro provided by this package is \stackengine. Nearly all other macros of this package merely provide an abbreviated invocation form of this macro, tailored for a particular application.

macros.name: stackinset
macros.doc: The macro \stackinset is for insetting smaller items (e.g., images or text) inside of a larger background items (e.g., images or text).

macros.name: stackMath
macros.doc: an invocation of \stackMath will change the default so that stackengine arguments will be processed in inline math mode (so-called \textstyle math).

macros.name: stackon
macros.doc: The \stackon and \stackunder macros are abbreviated forms of \stackengine in which the default values of parameters are taken. The only exception is the stacklength, which may be provided as an optional argument.

macros.name: stackText
macros.doc: an invocation of \stackText will reset the default processing of arguments to text mode.

macros.name: stacktype
macros.doc: The parameter \stacktype defaults to “S” (short stack) and defines the default type of stack to build.

macros.name: stackunder
macros.doc: The \stackon and \stackunder macros are abbreviated forms of \stackengine in which the default values of parameters are taken. The only exception is the stacklength, which may be provided as an optional argument.

macros.name: strutlongstacks
macros.doc: The mode \strutlongstacks, when set true (T), will automatically cause stackengine to condition each row of a long stack with a \strut during its construction (see §9 for more details).

macros.name: strutshortanchors
macros.doc: If a short stack is being created with a split anchor, the \strutshortanchors{} mode setting will determine whether the split occurs at the mid-height of the strutbox (“T”) or whether it will occur about the baseline (“F”).

macros.name: useanchorwidth
macros.doc: The parameter \useanchorwidth defaults to “F” (false) and indicates that, upon creation, the stack width should be taken as the widest element of the stack.

macros.name: Vectorstack
macros.doc: The \Centerstack macro has a math-mode equivalent called \Vectorstack, in which the stacking argument is automatically processed in math mode, regardless if whether the \stackMath mode is currently active.
